Not to mention the aura of positivity around her (cos of her words and behaviour) which made me feel completely relaxed and I knew I was not only in safe but highly professional hands.

Highly Recommended for professionalism, skill, positivity, and as the Best Eye Doctor!!

A very heartful Thank You once again Dr. Khyati Jain... You are Brilliant!!!

Glaucoma is dangerous because it is a "silent thief of sight."It slowly damages the eye's optic nerve, often without any early symptoms. By the time a person notices changes in their vision, the resulting damage is permanent and irreversible.The main dangers of the disease include:Irreversible Vision Loss: Once the optic nerve fibers are destroyed, they cannot be repaired or regenerated. Any vision lost to glaucoma is gone forever.No Early Warning Signs: The most common form (primary open-angle glaucoma) typically progresses painlessly. People usually lose their peripheral (side) vision first, which the brain easily compensates for, meaning they are unaware of the disease until it reaches advanced stages.Potential for Permanent Blindness: If left untreated, glaucoma continues to progress from peripheral vision loss to central vision loss and eventually to total blindness.Acute Medical Emergencies: A less common type angle-closure glaucoma, can cause sudden, dangerous spikes in eye pressure. This triggers severe eye pain, headaches, blurred vision, and nausea, and is considered an acute medical emergency that requires immediate treatment to prevent rapid blindness.As glaucoma cannot be cured, early detection through regular, comprehensive eye exams is the only way to catch it before irreversible damage occurs. If diagnosed early, treatments like eye drops, laser or surgery can lower eye pressure and save eye.

Intraocular lenses (IOLs) replace the natural eye lens during cataract surgery, with main types including monofocal (single-focus distance), premium multifocal (near/mid/far), Extended Depth of Focus (EDOF - continuous range), and Toric (astigmatism-correcting). Selection depends on lifestyle, prioritizing spectacle independence versus sharp, simple vision. 

Comparison of Main IOL Types

Monofocal IOLs: The standard, most common lens. Provides clear vision at one distance (usually far). Patients typically need reading glasses for near/intermediate tasks.
Multifocal IOLs: A "premium" lens with zones for near, intermediate, and far vision. These reduce or eliminate the need for glasses but may cause mild glare/halos at night.
Extended Depth of Focus (EDOF) IOLs: Creates a continuous range of high-quality vision rather than multiple set points. Provides excellent intermediate vision (computers) and improved distance over traditional multifocals with fewer glare issues.
Toric IOLs: Specifically designed to correct astigmatism. Available as monofocal, multifocal, or EDOF, ensuring sharp vision for those with irregularly shaped corneas.

He pioneered Phacoemulsification surgery (cataract surgery) in the north east suburbs of Mumbai, and continues to keep pace with the fast-evolving trends and developments in Ophthalmic science. Dr. Rai underwent basic medical training at LTMMC, Sion, Mumbai.
This was followed by a Masters Degree in Ophthalmology from MR Medical College, Gulbarga. After his basic training in Ophthalmology, Dr. Rai completed a fellowship at the prestigious Schell Eye Hospital, CMC, Vellore, under the tutelage of the renowned Prof. Ravi Thomas. Dr. Rai is at present focused on Refractive Lasik and Refractive Cataract Surgery.
